en: Fill in the symptom check again. Compare it to last week only to notice, not to judge.
Same as last week — record what was prescribed and what you missed.
Each week follows the same rhythm: a short check-in, one new skill to read about, and a small practice to carry into the week.
The sessions move from understanding ADHD, to organizing your life, to protecting your attention, to changing the thoughts that drive avoidance, and finally to keeping the gains.
You do not need to master a session before moving on. The skills layer — later weeks make sense because earlier ones prepared the ground, but showing up is enough.
Most people feel a pull to quit around the halfway point. The early relief fades, the hard work stays, and the new habit has not yet paid off.
That pull is normal and expected — it is not a sign the program is wrong for you. Plan now to notice it, and keep the practice small enough to keep doing.
Pick a single thing you want different by the end — one sentence. Keep it concrete and yours, not what anyone expects.
Run the week with your calendar and task list in place.
Each evening, note the one thing that went as planned and the one that didn't.
What is likely to get in the way this week, and what will you do when it happens?
